question: Within the same Palmer island and breeding season, do larger Adelie breeding groups produce more chicks per breeding pair than expected under equal per-pair productivity?
biological_hypothesis: Positive density dependence in reproductive output is expected under social facilitation or size-dependent protection, whereas equal per-pair productivity predicts chick totals proportional to breeding-pair counts.

analysis_frame.rows: Use outcome-bearing chick rows that pass the frozen five-island, positive-pair and study-derived season-key rules and match an adult-census colony transition in the same island and season.

observed_statistic.size: Within each island-season, z-standardize log1p adult-census breeding pairs.
observed_statistic.within_set_slope: OLS slope of productivity on standardized adult-census size; because size is mean-zero this equals sum(z_size * productivity) / sum(z_size^2).
observed_statistic.joint_statistic: Mean within-set slope with equal weight per island-season.

neutral_model.conditioning: Within each island-season hold fixed observed total chicks C and chick-dataset breeding-pair denominators d_i.
neutral_model.meaning: All breeding pairs have equal expected chick productivity; colony size affects expected chick count only through the number of pairs.
neutral_model.statistic_per_draw: Recompute productivity C_i/d_i and the same equal-weight mean within-set slope.

inference.p_value: one-sided upper-tail Monte Carlo p with +1 correction

sensitivities.chick_denominator_size: Repeat size predictor using z(log1p chick-dataset breeding pairs)) instead of the November adult-census size; require the same sign for a strong result.
sensitivities.prior_count_ge2: Repeat after requiring adult-census breeding pairs >= 2.
sensitivities.year_balance: Report per-island mean slopes and leave-one-island-out joint slopes.

interpretation.if_supported: Consistent with supra-proportional reproductive performance of larger breeding groups, a stronger signature of positive density dependence than extinction order alone.
interpretation.if_not_supported: Do not invoke social facilitation from the small-first extinction sequence; retain concentration as demographic reorganization unless another independent mechanism test succeeds.

boundaries: This test cannot distinguish social facilitation from correlated habitat quality, predation or other size-associated colony properties.
Do not replace the proportional multinomial null with a more favorable distribution after opening num_chicks.
Report this test regardless of whether it agrees with the simpler chicks-per-pair permutation gradient.
